parameters.name: ain
parameters.description: Effective inlet conversion coefficient: `ain*flow` adds pressure from metered air. Estimated jointly with the other independent coefficients at both fitting stages described below.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: Fraction of open-valve conductance assigned to `1-(valve/vfull)**3`; the complement multiplies `1-3*(valve/vfull)**2+2*(valve/vfull)**3`. Both basis functions decrease with closure and vanish at the seat. Estimated jointly at both stages.

parameters.name: gopen
parameters.description: Open-valve inertial conductance scale. Estimated jointly at both stages; no valve area or discharge coefficient is separately identifiable.

parameters.name: rvisc
parameters.description: Series linear pneumatic resistance converting pressure-rate discharge to pressure loss. Estimated jointly at both stages subject to `2 <= rvisc <= 30` s; the fitted value reaches the lower bound, so only a weakly determined low-pressure resistance is claimed.

parameters.name: tiny
parameters.description: Denominator safeguard, `tiny = 1e-12` bar, chosen solely to avoid a zero denominator at the fully closed seat and atmospheric pressure; negligible over measured pressure differences.

parameters.name: patm
parameters.description: Atmospheric reference pressure, `patm = 1` bar, supplied approximately by TASK.md and here assumed exactly; not adjusted to reduce simulation errors.

parameters.name: vfull
parameters.description: Fully closed valve normalization, `vfull = 100` %, from TASK.md. Clamping `Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)` restricts the conductance extension to the physical stroke.

parameters.name: back
parameters.description: Subatmospheric restoring rate, `back = 0.1` 1/s, chosen as a ten-second numerical vacuum-relaxation time, not estimated. `-back*Min(p-patm,0)` is a valve-independent extension outside normal pressurized operation, not an identified leak or a model of real reverse valve flow.

estimation.criterion: Final criterion: sum of squared free-run errors on pressure `p` in bar after each trajectory’s first sample, with no state correction. This matches long-horizon evaluation and avoids treating the filtered derivative `dp` as an independent instantaneous measurement. One-step pressure-transition squared error is only an initialization criterion.
estimation.data: Final coefficients use all 1452 rows of data/train.csv and all 1454 rows of data/val.csv as two separate trajectories, without joining their endpoints. There are 1451 and 1453 fitted pressure transitions. Initial samples set each free-run initial condition and are not residuals. The derivative column `dp` is not used for final estimation. The independent training-only comparison and first-two-thirds blocked comparison in fixed_atmosphere.py were used to assess structure generalization; only after these checks were both entire trajectories used to improve coefficient coverage. No rows were removed for outlier or transient handling and no test data were accessed.
estimation.method: Bound-constrained nonlinear least squares using the Trust Region Reflective algorithm in scipy.optimize.least_squares (SciPy 1.18.1). Reference: SciPy official least_squares documentation, checked in this round. Nonlinearity and physical bounds make a direct linear solution inapplicable. All four independent parameters were estimated together in each of two stages. First minimize squared one-step RK4 pressure-transition errors, starting at `ain = 0.0013` bar/(s*(l/min)), `gopen = 0.15` sqrt(bar)/s, `rvisc = 3` s, `weight = 0.4`; these broad positive guesses are close to preliminary mass-balance fit scales and avoid a vanishing-conductance start. That stage yielded `ain = 0.00121559303502` bar/(s*(l/min)), `gopen = 0.14005998302` sqrt(bar)/s, `rvisc = 2` s, `weight = 0.364873114204`. Then, starting at those values, minimize squared full free-run pressure errors and obtain `ain = 0.00126697375396` bar/(s*(l/min)), `gopen = 0.14285145806` sqrt(bar)/s, `rvisc = 2` s, `weight = 0.379625688673`. The numerical bounds were `0.0001 <= ain <= 0.005` bar/(s*(l/min)), `0.0001 <= gopen <= 0.4` sqrt(bar)/s, `2 <= rvisc <= 30` s and `0 <= weight <= 1`. Positive broad gain bounds avoid unphysical signs; the resistance lower bound limits the continuous restoring slope to at most `0.5` 1/s, avoiding an unresolved sub-sample outlet time scale in five-second RK4. The upper resistance bound allows slow, strongly viscous behavior. Both stages use two-point finite-difference Jacobians, `x_scale = "jac"`, linear loss, and relative stopping settings `ftol = 1e-11`, `xtol = 1e-11`, `gtol = 1e-11`; maximum function evaluations were 1000 and 1500 respectively, with actual solver counts 9 and 9. Each simulation is one classical RK4 step per `Ts = 5` s with the current logged inputs held constant. Numba 0.68.0 compiles the loops; no random sampling or seeds apply. Fixed and tied parameters are not optimization variables. The function guards excursions beyond 20 bar with a finite penalty; neither final fitted training trajectory approaches that guard.

discussion.family: Lumped isothermal ideal-gas inventory balance with a linear-plus-quadratic (Darcy–Forchheimer-type) series outlet resistance. The linear-plus-quadratic loss analogy, not a literal porous medium, motivates the resistance law; no particular publication was used for this structure.
discussion.interpretation: Pressure `p` is absolute pressure. The term `ain*flow` is the inlet contribution for an approximately isothermal gas inventory of fixed effective volume. Define the nonnegative overpressure `z = Max(p-patm,0)` bar and the valve conductance `g = (gopen*(weight*(1-(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)+(1-weight)*(1-3*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**2+2*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)))` in sqrt(bar)/s, with `weight` its monotone-basis fraction. If `u` is outlet discharge expressed as a pressure rate in bar/s, the assumed loss is `z = rvisc*u+(u/g)**2`; solving its positive root gives the implemented term `(gopen*(weight*(1-(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)+(1-weight)*(1-3*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**2+2*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)))*2*Max(p-patm,0)/(sqrt(4*Max(p-patm,0)+(rvisc*(gopen*(weight*(1-(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)+(1-weight)*(1-3*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**2+2*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3))))**2+tiny)+rvisc*(gopen*(weight*(1-(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3)+(1-weight)*(1-3*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**2+2*(Min(Max(valve,0),vfull)/vfull)**3))))`. This combines viscous resistance in the outlet piping with a valve-dependent inertial restriction; the assignment to individual hardware is not identifiable. The safeguard `tiny` has no physical meaning. At the fully closed seat the implemented outlet rate is exactly zero. The final term `-back*Min(p-patm,0)` restores numerical undershoots only; it is not reverse-flow physics.
discussion.origin: Started with linear relaxation, square-root discharge, compressible nozzle flow, positive pressure-power laws and power/exponential valve characteristics. Initial transition fits showed that near-square-root discharge substantially improved on linear pressure relaxation. Residuals by low pressure and valve opening motivated adding a series linear resistance instead of an arbitrary derivative offset: an offset would break zero-flow equilibrium. The linear-plus-quadratic pressure-drop structure came from physical reasoning, not symbolic search. The two monotone cubic valve basis functions are a deliberately parsimonious empirical stroke map. A third positive cubic basis coefficient converged essentially to zero in the exploratory fits and was removed. All coefficients in the delivered expression were then refitted, not copied from that exploratory fit.
discussion.limitations: The effective inlet volume, valve area, discharge coefficient, temperature, bubble holdup and calibration cannot be separated from these two pressure/input trajectories. No flow-delay, thermal or actuator state is present. On an independently simulated validation trajectory, the earlier training-only fit gave RMSE 0.038665 bar; first-two-thirds fits gave fresh-initialized tail RMSE 0.023717 bar on training and 0.057941 bar on validation. Final all-data refitting gave training RMSE 0.026168 bar and validation RMSE 0.037484 bar; these last two are fitting diagnostics, not independent validation. Final one-step residual correlations with the next-minus-current inlet-flow change are -0.807 on training and -0.716 on validation, showing missing timing/dynamics that the autonomous single-state form cannot resolve. Alternative future-flow diagnostic fits reduced transition errors but were excluded because future inputs are not arguments. The fully open and sealed endpoints are extrapolated: training stroke spans approximately 10.31 to 92.41 %, validation 1.63 to 94.45 %. The subatmospheric term has no identified physical validity. Absolute pressures far outside the observed approximately 0.99 to 2.19 bar range, thermal transients, liquid-level changes and negative inlet flows are not validated. The resistance `rvisc` reaches its 2 s bound; its estimate is partly determined by the chosen time-resolution safeguard, not a resolved pipe measurement. R1: `ain > 0`, so increasing `flow` always increases `dp`. R2: for `0 <= weight <= 1`, both cubic stroke basis functions are nonincreasing in closure, the pressure-drop discharge is nonnegative, and the subatmospheric term does not depend on closure; hence increasing `valve` cannot decrease `dp`, including in the implemented vacuum extension. R3: at `flow = 0` and `p = patm`, all terms vanish, with `patm = 1` bar. R4: for any not-fully-closed valve and `flow = 0`, `dp < 0` above `patm` and `dp > 0` below it, so atmospheric equilibrium is attractive. R5: at `valve = vfull`, the conductance is exactly zero, so for `flow >= 0` the derivative `ain*flow-back*Min(p-patm,0)` is nonnegative. No unexplained outlet leak remains at the sealed seat. These are structural properties, not conclusions inferred just from observed samples.
